title: The strict cardinal estimate needs a separate countable-cardinal case.
details: Andrew Marks, Set Theory, revision 2026-01-31, Theorem26.2, printed/PDF p.104. The proof treats an infinite cardinal kappa and alpha<kappa, then writes that the union of alpha countable possible-value sets has cardinality at most omega times |alpha| < kappa. The displayed strict estimate fails when kappa=omega and alpha is a nonzero finite ordinal: omega times |alpha|=omega. The cardinal-preservation theorem remains true. Repair: finite cardinals and omega are preserved by transitive-model finite/ordinal absoluteness; apply the union-cardinality argument only for uncountable kappa, where max(aleph0,|alpha|)<kappa. This also retains validity at singular uncountable cardinals, without the invalid supremum estimate recorded separately in UNGER-03. Corpus disposition: forcing-chain-conditions#cardinal-preservation adopts the repaired union-cardinality proof, explicitly handling finite and countable cardinals separately; #singular-bound-question explains why an unbounded union below a singular cardinal does not defeat the cardinality estimate. The source itself has not been corrected.
